rcore.statement: Every crisis becomes evidence. Every replay improves readiness. Every cycle strengthens resilience.
rcore.law: R-CORE is not the crisis application; it is the recursive operational architecture beneath it. No commit without a named human-authority event (MODE_R-CORE_SPEC).

nose.needs: Restore electricity / operations quickly while understanding impact, available backup capacity, community and facility needs, and who is responsible.
outcomes: Every need outside the grid (a facility without power, a plant without water, a neighbourhood without heat) is recorded, prioritized and assigned to a verified responder
Scarce backup capacity (generators, fuel, crews, shelters) is allocated against recorded needs, not requests by loudness
Every plan change carries who authorized it and why; the workforce and the public read the current plan
The event replays for the next one
nose.solution: DRS beside GridOS: GridOS restores the grid; DRS runs the verified roster, needs intake, resource allocation, plan versioning, polling and replay for the human and organizational crisis around it.

risks.issue: A false responder receives authority or resources
risks.mitigation: Verified roster with rank / authority; every grant is a named-human row; unauthorized requests refused and recorded

risks.issue: A recommendation is acted on as a decision
risks.mitigation: AI recommends and organizes; authorized humans retain command; no commit without a named human-authority event (R-CORE)

risks.issue: Needs intake carries names, locations, medical and welfare facts of affected people
risks.mitigation: Minimum record (CASPER-shaped fields), role-scoped reads, retention by event, no public row ever carries a person's medical detail

risks.issue: A public plan view can be quoted out of context or spoofed
risks.mitigation: Controlled transparency: every public statement carries the authorizing role and the plan version; corrections are versions, never deletions

risks.issue: A request from an unverified party diverts scarce supplies
risks.mitigation: Allocation only against a recorded need by a verified responder; every grant is a named-human row; refusals recorded

risks.issue: GridOS / hospital / notification systems each have their own data and access model
risks.mitigation: Coordinate beside them (MVP 1 needs no integration); cross-system ingestion is MVP 3 and enters only through the de-risk gate

risks.issue: Networks and power fail in the events the product exists for
risks.mitigation: Phone-first, offline-tolerant record with replay on reconnect; the four-channel delivery precedent from the polling engine

risks.issue: Public buyers move by cycle and grant, not by pilot
risks.mitigation: Pilot through an existing operator's or partner's authority; readiness subscription priced after the S16 pilot; align with THIRA/SPR reporting cycles

risks.issue: Regional health data crosses institutions and jurisdictions
risks.mitigation: Healthcare pilot carries only capacity and coordination facts, no patient records, until compliance counsel signs the data map

risks.issue: A crisis-coordination system is a target during the crisis
risks.mitigation: Verified roster + signed rows + append-only record; the amber→red two-step for every consequential act; incident-response drills through HSEEP

risks.issue: A wrong recommendation or a stale plan version is acted on
risks.mitigation: AI recommends and organizes, authorized humans retain command; every plan carries who authorized it and when; replay reconstructs what was known

crs.name: Verified authority + roster
crs.in: DRS-01.01.IN — a responder, official or volunteer is admitted only after verification by a named authority; rank / authority is on the record
crs.out: DRS-01.01.OUT — 100% of grants carry the verifier's identity and time; an unverified request is refused and recorded (target set after the baseline pilot)

crs.name: Needs intake
crs.in: DRS-02.01.IN — any affected person or field responder can submit a need (heat, shelter, water, transport, capacity) from a phone in ≤ 3 taps
crs.out: DRS-02.01.OUT — every need has a timestamp, a location, a priority and a state (open / assigned / fulfilled)
crs.evidence: DECLARED (intake record shaped on CDC CASPER + FEMA Community Lifelines — see needsAssessment)

crs.name: Resource inventory + gap analysis
crs.in: DRS-03.01.IN — resources, facilities and supplies are listed with quantity, location, owner and qualification
crs.out: DRS-03.01.OUT — a live gap view: needs open vs resources available, per scenario
crs.evidence: DECLARED (ICS 215 / NIMS resource typing — see needsAssessment)

crs.name: Assignment + fulfilment
crs.in: DRS-04.01.IN — an authorized person assigns a resource to a need; the assignee acknowledges; fulfilment is confirmed by the need's owner
crs.out: DRS-04.01.OUT — need → assignment and assignment → fulfilment times recorded for 100% of needs

crs.name: Plan versioning + authority traceability
crs.in: DRS-05.01.IN — Plan v1 → Event → Change → Authority → Plan v2; every change names its authorizer
crs.out: DRS-05.01.OUT — the user reads what changed, why, who authorized it, what to do now; an unversioned change cannot exist

crs.name: Collective intelligence (eXeL polling)
crs.in: DRS-06.01.IN — concerns and priorities are collected from the workforce / public through eXeL polling sessions (33 languages, phone-first)
crs.out: DRS-06.01.OUT — themes (3/6/9) with summaries feed the plan revision; time from concern to revision recorded
crs.evidence: SOURCED (the eXeL AI Polling engine exists: Cubes 1–9)

crs.name: Controlled public transparency
crs.in: DRS-07.01.IN — the public / workforce reads the current plan, its version and its authority; nothing more
crs.out: DRS-07.01.OUT — acknowledgement rate of each revision measured

crs.name: Three resource plans
crs.in: DRS-08.01.IN — Conservative / Baseline / Aggressive plans with assumptions, cost, resources and the trigger for changing plans
crs.out: DRS-08.01.OUT — the plan in force and its trigger are visible at all times; a plan change is a versioned, authorized event

crs.name: Operational record + replay (R-CORE)
crs.in: DRS-09.01.IN — every mark, grant, assignment, change and refusal is one canonical row; the record replays
crs.out: DRS-09.01.OUT — replay reconstructs who knew what, who authorized what, what changed, what moved, what happened; replay hash stable
crs.evidence: SOURCED (R-CORE spec; the Drone-2525 domain play carries a working replay hash and register)

crs.name: Simulation + qualification
crs.in: DRS-10.01.IN — the three scenarios run against the record; readiness is measured
crs.out: DRS-10.01.OUT — simulation vs actual performance reported per event

crs.name: Cross-system ingestion
crs.in: DRS-11.01.IN — GridOS / Veoci / Sentinel / CrisisCommand facts and events enter the record with provenance; DRS never replaces them
crs.out: DRS-11.01.OUT — an ingested fact carries its source and time; conflicts are shown, not resolved silently

crs.name: Three interfaces
crs.in: DRS-12.01.IN — phone portrait, phone landscape, desktop landscape / full screen
crs.out: DRS-12.01.OUT — every workflow completes at 390 px wide and in landscape; gated in CI like the 2525 domain plays
crs.evidence: SOURCED (the 2525 harness runs both orientations in CI)

crs.name: Validation + evidence program
crs.in: DRS-13.01.IN — the thirteen S16 metrics are the columns of every pilot record
crs.out: DRS-13.01.OUT — WTP ranges and NBA deltas are written only from measured pilot columns

needsAssessment.ask: research best in class needs assessments to help fiends business (operator 2026-09-23)
needsAssessment.law: Two families are needed and they are not the same instrument: the CUSTOMER needs assessment prices the product (S3, S8–S10, S13, S14); the CRISIS needs assessment is the product's own intake (DRS-02, DRS-03, S4, S15, S16). Every method below is SOURCED by URL; what DRS takes from it is DECLARED.

methods.name: Outcome-Driven Innovation (Ulwick / Strategyn)
methods.what: Jobs-to-be-done put into practice: 50–150 desired-outcome statements per job, each {direction, measure, object, context}; the opportunity algorithm ranks importance vs satisfaction; segments are formed by outcome profile, not by industry
methods.whatDrsTakes: Every S13 value-driver row and every S14 interview question is written as a desired-outcome statement; the S3 segmentation is validated by outcome profile (the X/Y/Z weights are the first three outcome clusters)

methods.name: Voice of the Customer loop (the gate-review template's own method)
methods.what: Continuous and iterative customer feedback through the stage gates: understand needs vs the next-best alternative → validate concepts with prototypes → evaluate and adapt
methods.whatDrsTakes: The G1→G2 program: three segments × interviews vs the paired NBA before any prototype; the S11/S15/S17 VOC tables of the Pod carry the results

methods.name: Kano classification
methods.what: Must-be · performance · delighter attributes from paired functional/dysfunctional questions; a must-be is not a differentiator
methods.whatDrsTakes: The 'not differentiators' list (alerting, dashboards, incident logs, messaging, simulations, AAR) are must-be for the NBAs; each S13 row is tagged must-be / performance / delighter in the S16 interviews before it is priced

families.name: Crisis / community needs assessment (the product's intake)

methods.name: CDC CASPER — Community Assessment for Public Health Emergency Response
methods.what: Rapid needs assessment at the household level: two-stage cluster sampling (30 clusters × 7 households), volunteer interview teams, a standard questionnaire, results in days; toolkit 3rd edition 2019
methods.whatDrsTakes: DRS-02 needs intake carries CASPER's record shape (who · where · what is lacking · severity · who is responsible · time) so a phone poll is a valid sample of a community, not a shout; the 30×7 design is the fallback when the roster cannot reach everyone

methods.name: UN OCHA MIRA — Multi-Sector Initial Rapid Assessment
methods.what: One common picture across all sectors: situational analysis within 72 hours, MIRA report within two weeks, agreed immediate strategies
methods.whatDrsTakes: The S4 CONOPS clock: authoritative facts and a first needs picture within 72 h; one picture shared by command, responders and the affected population (S6 layers)

methods.name: FEMA THIRA / SPR — Threat and Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment / Stakeholder Preparedness Review
methods.what: Capability targets and the resource requirements to meet them, self-assessed yearly against last year's capability (built, sustained, lost)
methods.whatDrsTakes: S15's Conservative / Baseline / Aggressive plans are expressed as capability targets with resource requirements; the trigger for changing plans is a target missed

methods.name: FEMA HSEEP — Homeland Security Exercise and Evaluation Program
methods.what: Exercise design, evaluation and corrective actions that feed the next cycle, informed by risk and capability assessments
methods.whatDrsTakes: S16's Replay → Improve columns are HSEEP corrective actions; the R-CORE loop is HSEEP's cycle with the record kept by the system instead of a binder

methods.name: FEMA Community Lifelines
methods.what: Eight lifelines (Safety and Security · Food, Hydration, Shelter · Health and Medical · Energy · Communications · Transportation · Hazardous Materials · Water) with a status ladder Unstable → Stabilizing → Recovery
methods.whatDrsTakes: The 'what people currently need' list on S2 and the needs-intake categories are the eight lifelines; a lifeline status is the first line of every plan version

methods.name: NIMS resource typing + ICS 215 Operational Planning Worksheet
methods.what: Resources categorized by capability; the ICS 215 lists assignments, resources required vs available and the gap for the next operational period
methods.whatDrsTakes: DRS-03 resource inventory + gap analysis is an ICS 215 the responders fill from phones; DRS-04 assignments use NIMS typing so a request names a capability, not a brand

methods.name: ISO 22301 Business Impact Analysis
methods.what: Critical activities, maximum acceptable downtime, resources required, financial and non-financial impact of disruption
methods.whatDrsTakes: SEG-1's outcome units (outage-hour, production-hour) come from the buyer's own BIA; the S14 interview asks for the BIA's downtime and impact figures before naming any price
